_note: Keystone seed — ALGORITHM nodes + task-scoped better_than edges. Algorithms are already captured as project capability facets, so these match via facets (not deps). 'better' is strongly task/constraint-scoped and CONDITIONAL — the user may have chosen the simpler algorithm deliberately (interpretability, small data), so the edge always names the condition under which the upgrade wins. Loser node names match real facet labels exactly so they fire.

solutions.name: learned-to-rank
solutions.description: LambdaMART / gradient-boosted ranking trained on labeled outcomes.

solutions.name: a-star pathfinding
solutions.description: A* heuristic shortest-path search, recomputed per query.

solutions.name: contraction hierarchies
solutions.description: Precomputed shortcut hierarchy for near-instant repeated shortest-path queries on a static graph.

solutions.name: k-means
solutions.description: Centroid clustering; assumes spherical, equal-size clusters, needs k.

solutions.name: hdbscan
solutions.description: Density clustering: finds variable-density clusters + noise, no k.

better_than.task: ranking WHEN you have labeled outcome data
better_than.source: learned-to-rank (LambdaMART) beats hand-weighted KNN once you have outcome labels to train on; KNN stays fine for cold-start / no labels

better_than.task: MANY repeated shortest-path queries on a mostly-static graph
better_than.source: contraction hierarchies precompute shortcuts for orders-of-magnitude faster repeated queries; A* is better for one-off queries or fast-changing graphs

better_than.task: sequence modeling WHEN you have lots of data and don't need interpretability
better_than.source: neural sequence models beat HMMs with enough data; HMMs stay better for small-data / interpretable / explicit-state cases

better_than.task: clustering with noise or variable-density clusters and unknown k
better_than.source: HDBSCAN handles noise + variable density + no preset k; k-means is fine for known-k spherical clusters
dense embeddings capture meaning; tf-idf only shared terms — but tf-idf is better for exact-keyword / rare-term matching
